newsitem.title: USA: Clinton thanks supporters, enjoys star-studded gala.
newsitem.headline: Clinton thanks supporters, enjoys star-studded gala.

text.p: A thankful President Bill Clinton used the last hours before his second term begins to go to church twice on Sunday, touch base with his supporters and relax at a star-studded gala concert in his honour.

Washington was in a celebratory mood, with thousands of Democratic faithful and others who came to witness the inauguration on Monday doing a lot of party-hopping, touring monuments and braving frigid temperatures to attend a tent festival on the Mall.

The Clintons and Vice President Al Gore and his family joined 11,000 of their closest friends -- who have paid up to $3,000 each -- for a Presidential Gala concert at the USAir Arena in Landover, Maryland. The entertainment lineup included Gloria Estefan, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Aretha Franklin, Whoopi Goldberg, the Dave Matthews Band, Kenny G, Bernadette Peters, Kenny Rogers, James Taylor and Stevie Wonder.

But 24 hours before his second inauguration, Clinton seemed focused on spiritual renewal and remembering how far he had come from two years ago, when many pundits thought the election of a Republican-majority Congress signalled he would be limited to one term in the White House.
"I actually, in the darkest days of 1994 and '95, always believed that we would be doing this on this day," Clinton told a brunch meeting of the Democratic National Committee.

"I've run my last race, but we haven't done all the work we need to do for our country, for the 21st century. We have to maintain both a commitment to progress and a commitment to community," Clinton said.

These days, Clinton's public approval ratings are soaring above the 60 percent mark. But he also faces numerous investigations into his business, political and private affairs which could sour his second term.

Clinton will take the oath of office at noon (1700 GMT) on Monday on the steps of the U.S. Capitol, the 53rd time the ceremony has been enacted. White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the president was still working on the speech he will deliver to an expectant nation.

Clinton gave a sneak preview of his address in brief remarks to the audience at the conclusion of Sunday's two-hour gala, thanking the young performers for their part in building a bridge to the 21st century.

"Tomorrow we will not just celebrate our democracy, we must renew it," Clinton told the exuberant crowd. "Tomorrow we'll be preparing our nation for a brand new century and a brand new millenium with brand new adventures and mountains to climb for all future genertations of Americans."

The president seemed impressed by the crowds that turned out for the festival, "An American Journey," on the Mall of Washington monuments over the weekend despite the icy weather, which made them rush from tent to tent like students changing classes at a makeshift college in the far north.

"I see the pictures of all the thousands and thousands of people in the shivering cold who were out on the Mall yesterday, all the children taking in the exhibits, and sensed the freedom and the feeling and the enthusiasm in the streets -- maybe this will be better the second time around," he told the Democratic National Committee gathering.
Clinton's wife Hillary also spoke on Sunday to a gathering of Democrats known as "Emily's List," a grassroots organisation of donors that raises money for women candidates.

Mrs. Clinton said she thought some of the issues featured in Clinton's second presidential campaign, such as family leave, gun control and curfews for teenagers, signalled not the "feminization" of politics but the "humanization" of politics.

On Sunday morning the Clintons attended two church services. First they went to Columbia Baptist church, where the pastor from Clinton's home church in Arkansas, Rex Horne, was guest speaker. Later they visited the church they regularly attend, Foundry United Methodist Church.
The Clintons and daughter Chelsea appeared delighted by the impressive line-up of stars saluting the president at the Sunday evening concert.

Goldberg reminded the audience that Clinton would be taking his oath on the holiday commemorating the birthday of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., and said he would continue King's work with "an irresistible call to this nation to rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed."
